answer.evidence: The sign is a tall, flat, face-on board seen from the front. The header at rows 0-8 is drawn as a front-facing strip: row 1 is a light highlight and row 2 a mid-green, then a white label panel at rows 3-5, a mid-green row 6, and dark rows 7-8. That is at most a 1-2 row rim, with no ellipse and no clear front-edge line followed by an eave shadow. The board at rows 9-28 is a vertical face carrying the white text. The silhouette is nearly constant at 14-16 px wide, with no widening and narrowing that would suggest a top surface. No receding side face is drawn. The base at rows 29-31 is a thin dark strip, so the object has no top surface of 3+ rows and reads as front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a vertical green sign with a lighter cap and white vertical lettering. It has 8 visible tones per tile, above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills, against 9% for the bus shelter. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, which matches the references. The outline is a dark green tint beside the green body, not a black sticker line. The body has about 4 green steps (highlight edge, mid, dark, deep outline) plus the white text, one or two steps fewer than the richer references. The lettering and edge highlights give some surface variation, though there is little grain. Density is slightly below kiosk-a and vending-a but at or above bus-shelter-a, which is accepted shipped art. A careful artist would accept it next to the references, so it passes narrowly.
